catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class expresses closing or opening the output of a DC power supply: cap.device.configure.v1 writes named state parameters only, and cap.actuation.gpio.v1 is bound to io.gpio/io.digital pins, not to a supply output.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposed ScpiDriver/family-config. The GPP-4323 profile writes are VSET1:<value> and ISET1:<value> with no separator before the value; the SCPI command-table tokenizer takes the text before the first space, ?, { or (, so the literal wire token cannot be matched against the clone without changing the wire syntax. The package is therefore a direct Driver over drivers:PowerSupply with a native.py factory. NOT COVERED: the repository's Multimeter class and the four multimeter profiles (rigol_dm3068.json, akip_2101.json, akip_b778.json), and the unused SwitchController/STM32 switch board; this package serves only the GPP-4323 power supply. The switch controller has no profile in the clone and its docstring says it is not used yet. The profile's command table has no VSET1?/ISET1? entries, although its notes confirm the readback; native.py adds those two command names so the driver's setpoint reads reach the instrument, and that hardware path was not run. The current limit declares only the sourced maximum 3.0 A; no line of the clone states a lower bound. The example site overlay narrows the voltage to 60 V and the current to 20 mA. Every Fact and Limit cites a line of the clone at the pinned commit; G4 emitted no warning. At R1 the loader does not refuse the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package (that refusal is R2/R3 only), and this package did not run any hardware backend.
